items.title: Hal Espinosa interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 20, 2024
items.q: He was the one that motivated me to start practicing.

ctx.x: Yes. I actually started when I was eleven. I went and saw a movie when I was in the seventh grade and it was Harry James, and he was the feature. He was the guy that was the focal point, and his band. And I remember Dick Haymes I think was in it and then a girl singer. And I went away wanting to play a trumpet because Harry was in front of the band playing. He won the singer away from I think Dick Haymes, whoever the other boy singer was. I went home and asked my dad, you know, if I could get a trumpet. So he…

good player, I was just in the ninth grade. So the high school in Riverside, there’s only one high school, Riverside Polytechnic High. And they had a great band and they had — there were three junior high schools that fed into the high school so they picked all three first chair junior high players to put in the advanced band. So I was next to last chair. And they were supposed to have a concert the next day at an elementary school, you know, a big thing for us. And so the trumpet player, the first trumpet…
I love that because there’s two spots in that story where I thought it was going somewhere and it didn’t. I thought you know it finally got to you and you played it beautifully.
